title: Photosynthesis: how green plants make food
subject: science
strengths: Most of the class can name the leaf, stem and roots and say what each part does.
The class can state the photosynthesis recipe: light, water and carbon dioxide become food and oxygen.

modelAnswers.question: Name the three main parts of a green plant and give the job of each part.
modelAnswers.answer: The leaf catches light, the stem holds the plant up, and the roots drink in water from the soil.

modelAnswers.question: A plant is kept in the dark all night. Which process is still happening in its leaves, and what does that process do?
modelAnswers.answer: Respiration is still happening: it breaks down food with oxygen to release energy.

commonErrors.misconception: Only animals breathe; plants do not.
commonErrors.example: A learner writes on the worksheet that a plant cannot breathe because it has no nose.

fixIt.prompt: Fix it: say how a plant takes in and gives out gases without a nose.
fixIt.corrected: Corrected working: plants take in and give out gases too - they respire all the time, day and night.

commonErrors.misconception: Only animals breathe; plants do not.
commonErrors.example: On the exit ticket, a learner says respiration stops at night when the light goes out.

fixIt.prompt: Fix it: rewrite the sentence so respiration carries on at night instead of stopping.
fixIt.corrected: Corrected check: respiration runs all the time, day and night, to release energy from food.

nextSteps: Reteach the trap, landing that plants take in and give out gases too: they respire all the time, day and night.
